product.reading: Reading the playbooks and their runs.

overviewPage.description: When one product sees something, a playbook acts through the others. Steps that change something important wait for a person.
overviewPage.waitingDetail: They go on once someone approves, and stop if refused.
overviewPage.noConnectionsDetail: Steps call products and webhooks an admin adds under Connections, and nothing else.
overviewPage.last30DaysDetail: Green when every run of the day was done, amber when some failed, red when all did.

playbooksPage.description: What starts each playbook, and the steps it takes.

playbookPage.newDescription: Write the playbook as JSON: its trigger, the conditions on the event, and its steps.
playbookPage.stepsDetail: In order. A step reads the answers of the steps before it.
playbookPage.tryItDetail: An event as the trigger would send it. A dry run sends nothing and shows what each step would send.
playbookPage.definitionDetail: trigger, conditions and steps as JSON; the API reference describes each step. Runs already started keep the steps they started with.

runsPage.description: Every run, with what each step sent and what came back.
runsPage.noneDetail: A run starts when a trigger fires, or when someone runs a playbook.

runPage.notFoundDetail: It may have been deleted after the retention.
runPage.waitsForEditor: An editor can approve or refuse it.
runPage.stepsDetail: What each step sent, without the token, and what came back.
runPage.dryDetail: A dry run: nothing was sent. Values that come from earlier steps are empty.

approvalsPage.description: Runs waiting for a person before a step that changes something important.
approvalsPage.noneDetail: Runs that reach an approval step wait here.

connectionsPage.description: The only addresses steps call: OpenAsy products with an API token, and Slack, Teams or other webhooks. Tokens and webhook keys are kept sealed and never shown again.
connectionsPage.addDetail: For a product, an API token made in that product with the role its steps need: editor to open incidents, admin to suspend people.
connectionsPage.name: Name

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this automation.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this automation, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also write and run playbooks and approve steps; admins also add connections, delete playbooks, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
